fact: A study published in 2021 of three Libyan local authorities (Misurata, Sabratha and Rujban) found that access to the internet at their offices was not always available — in Sabratha's finance department, where fifteen computers were on a client/server network, the internet was 'often disconnected and unreliable', and in Rujban it was 'normally unavailable' — that no authority had an effective cross-authority network, and that staff worked in standalone in-house or third-party systems, with online services used only occasionally to update the authority's website.
title: E-government and digital transformation in Libyan local authorities
publisher: International Journal of Teaching and Case Studies (University of Gloucestershire ePrints)
